integration_decision.name: SEPARATE_CURRENT_SHA_DIAGNOSTIC_FROM_FUTURE_SERIALIZATION_ACCEPTANCE
integration_decision.finding: Earlier A-paused/B-must-finish-before-release requirement is a valid current-SHA race-reproduction diagnostic but an invalid universal post-fix acceptance condition: a correct transaction-wide publication lock can intentionally block B until A is released. Requiring B to finish during A pause would reject a safe serialized implementation. runner.py currently writes latest.json, audit_latest.json, anata_latest.json separately with no surrounding publication lock; existing preflight runs children sequentially. Race still unproven.
integration_decision.runnable_no_network_contract: For pinned current-SHA diagnostic: spawn A on empty archive, pause A immediately before third output write via spawn-safe bounded Events, verify first two A outputs and absent A handoff, append PIT-visible BTC ETF rowB (T=1700000000000; effective=T-2000, available=observed=T-1000; source=farside_etf, source_record_id=rowB), spawn B on same directory; if B completes while A paused, verify B generation via coverage/audit counts/rowB provenance and snapshot all three B JSON, then release A and assert final three-file coherence; mixed B latest/audit with stale A handoff => FAIL (defect reproduced). For future fixed-SHA acceptance, DO NOT require B completion before release: assert B started, release A within bounded timeout, join A/B, require B's rowB generation is last coherently published or a proven stale-write suppression mechanism leaves all three B; no mixed generations. B waiting for A's publication lock is allowed, but post-release timeout/deadlock => FAIL. In both cases missing barrier, rowB delta, valid JSON, process exitcodes, cleanup or final generation proof => INVALID_TEST, never PASS. Use compact IPC, finally release/terminate/join, no network/sleeps/mock handoff. Re-pin and revalidate on any new HEAD.
